subject: Mid‑quarter trajectory brief + runway compression asks
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Nathan Reed <n.reed@atlascloud.com>, procurement@atlascloud.com
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid‑quarter trajectory brief + runway compression asks

Team — attaching a short readout for Wednesday’s bridgeboard. Key points up front:

1) OKR status highlights (current quarter)
- Feature: Dedicated pilot onboarding — on track for GA trial with AtlasCloud; onboarding tasks at 72% complete.
- Performance: Rollout 1 reduced gen P95 to ~340ms in staging (target 300ms by QBR).
- Cost efficiency: Initial batching + quantization saved ~18% token cost vs baseline.

2) What’s at risk / why we need exec help
- Runway compression: We need to compress the pilot timeline by two weeks to hit AtlasCloud’s procurement window (they require production token volumes by 9/1).
- Dependencies: infra needs a capacity carve‑out (4 x A100-equivalent) approved; security needs to sign a scoped SOC/PCI memo for pilot data handling; legal needs a one‑page SLA exception signed for the pilot period.

3) Asks (owners + due dates)
- Markus: can you approve a short‑term capacity reservation (4GPUs) by Tue, 7/14? This will enable the accelerated pilot test.
- Laura: can you expedite the SLA exception review with Legal — request by 7/16? I attached the draft form.
- Vanessa: please confirm exec alignment and whether we can commit a small credit (up to $15k) to remove friction on procurement.

Attachments: QBR-deck-v2.pptx (summary slide + migration plan), SLA-exception-form.pdf

I’ll be on the bridgeboard at 11:30 to walk the three slides and surface the blockers. Short, focused asks — want to avoid a long docket item.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Nathan Reed <n.reed@atlascloud.com>, procurement@atlascloud.com
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid‑quarter trajectory brief + runway compression asks

Thanks Aditya — the summary is clear. A couple quick notes: 

- I agree we should compress the runway if AtlasCloud’s procurement window is fixed. I can advocate for the $15k credit but want confirmation on what it covers (tokens vs support hours). Please add a one‑line in the deck.
- Markus — can you confirm capacity availability? If not A100s, what’s our compatible fallback (e.g., 8xA10s or equivalent)? We need concrete options to present.
- Laura — if Legal can push the SLA exception to 7/16, I will escalate to Chief Legal for a signoff call.

Small ask for Aditya: can you drop a short bullet in the deck showing the risk if we do NOT compress (expected slip to GA +6 weeks; revenue impact estimate)? That will help the bridgeboard prioritize.

Vanessa Ortiz
VP, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Nathan Reed <n.reed@atlascloud.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid‑quarter trajectory brief + runway compression asks

Aditya / team — quick infra update:

- 4xA100 short‑term carve is feasible from capacity planning, but it will require moving one dedicated pool (Team X) to spot for a 3‑week window. That has knock‑on effects documented in my note; I’ll share the schedule in the drive.
- Fallback: we can provision 8xA10 for the pilot with an estimated 10–15% slower P95; that is acceptable for discovery but not for AtlasCloud’s SLA ask.

I’ll commit to confirming the physical carve by EOD Mon 7/13 if Leadership approves the swap. If we need a hard guarantee earlier, we’ll need to surface the tradeoff to Team X and Ops.

On the SLA exception: I reviewed the draft. Redlines are minor — LGTM from infra side.

—Markus
Head of Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Nathan Reed <n.reed@atlascloud.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid‑quarter trajectory brief + runway compression asks

Aditya / team — thanks for the clear brief and for surfacing the asks. A few items from AtlasCloud: 

- Procurement timeline: we can sign the pilot SOW on 8/01 but need production capacity validation by 8/15. Compressing two weeks off your timeline would make a big difference.
- On the credit: procurement can accept a capped implementation credit that applies to first‑month usage. $15k is within scope; we’ll document it in the SOW.
- Security: our InfoSec will need the scoped SOC memo and a quick Q&A (30 minutes). We can make time the week of 7/20 if your Security org can commit.

Next steps I need from you by 7/16: final confirmation on capacity carve (4xA100 or fallback), one‑page SLA exception signed, and a short risk paragraph for our procurement committee. If you can deliver those, I’ll push the internal timelines to meet 8/01 signoff.

Thanks — Nathan
Nathan Reed
Head of Cloud Platform Partnerships
AtlasCloud

On Fri, Jul 10, 2026 at 09:12 AM Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com> wrote:
